title: MMBench-Live: A Continuously Evolving Benchmark for Multimodal Models
claim: A multi-agent pipeline turns a static benchmark into structured specs, fresh task-aware data, and verified QA, so it can be updated automatically.
layout: 4 numbered dashed panels in a loop, orange arrows, agent labels on top
description: A four-stage flow drawn as numbered dashed rounded panels, linked by orange block arrows. Panel 1 (top left) shows the inputs: the original MMBench paper PDF, a sample dataset item (a dog image with a multiple-choice question), and a user request to update the dataset. Panel 2 (top right) is the Benchmark Summary Agent. It derives text descriptions from the paper and visual patterns from sampled dataset images, and merges them into a Structured Benchmark Description. Panel 3 (bottom right) is the Data Acquisition Agent. A task-aware planner holds site, query and task sets, which feed three retrieval strategies shaded orange, purple and yellow. Retrieved images go through feedback and filtering, with a regenerate loop and a database of image-text pairs. Panel 4 (bottom left) is the QA Generation Agent. It generates a question over a portrait and sends it to a step-by-step executable verification chain, ending in MMBench-Live. Pale blue and pink fills and cartoon icons carry the eye through the panels.
caption: Overview of the MMBench-Live framework. MMBench-Live is constructed by converting the original MMBench into structured descriptions, acquiring new data in a task-aware manner, and generating executable and verified QA pairs for evaluation.
abstract: Evaluation benchmarks are essential for assessing vision-language models (VLMs), but most multimodal benchmarks are static, making them vulnerable to temporal staleness, data contamination, and costly maintenance. We present MMBench-Live, a continuously evolving multimodal benchmark built by a multi-agent-driven automated pipeline. Our framework treats benchmark evolution as task-guided dataset construction, integrating structured benchmark specification, feedback-controlled real-time data acquisition, and verifiable QA generation with executable reasoning. To maintain cross-version comparability, we introduce a distribution-consistent update strategy that extracts task-related visual patterns from the original benchmark to guide data collection and filtering. Instantiated from MMBench, MMBench-Live contains 5.9K newly generated evaluation instances with a high answer correctness rate, while each update costs about USD 30 and takes 1-2 hours. Extensive evaluations show that MMBench-Live preserves stable model rankings, maintains semantic alignment with the original benchmark, and exhibits weaker contamination-related memorization signals, suggesting a practical and scalable paradigm for sustainable multimodal benchmark evolution. The project is available at https://github.com/PRIS-CV/MMBench-Live.
